processing: A cultivar rather than a finished tea. The processing follows whichever tea its leaf goes into.
harvest_season: Buds in mid-March and is ready to pick in mid-April.
appearance_dry: Depends on the tea made from it; the fresh shoots are yellow-green, pointed and sturdy.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the tea made; as a green tea, typically a light yellow-green.
appearance_wet: The growing leaf is long and pale green with a flat, smooth surface, about 9.2 by 3.3 cm.
taste_profile: No tasting record specific to this cultivar is well established; the cup depends on the tea made from it.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Chinese green tea made from it; follow the tea's own style if it was made otherwise.

vintage_note: Seldom sold under its own name. Its leaf goes into regional teas, sold according to their class; green teas are usually the current spring harvest.
description:
Zhuyeqi No. 9 is a bush cultivar grown across Hunan's tea areas, one of a family of selections carrying the Zhuyeqi name. You are more likely to meet it in a garden than on a tea list.

The bush has a half-open habit, with long, pale green, smooth leaves. It buds in mid-March and is picked from mid-April, and its shoots are yellow-green and sturdy, concentrated in the upper canopy, with one bud and three leaves averaging 0.7 g.

There is no well-established taste profile of its own, since the result depends on what the maker does with the leaf. Brew it according to the style of tea you have bought.

Growers like it for drought and cold tolerance and for cuttings that take well, at a reported 94.5% survival. It has also been planted in Anhui, Hubei, Jiangxi and Sichuan.
history: Little is documented about its breeding and release. It is recorded mainly as a Hunan cultivar that later spread to several other provinces.
